messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — SEV2: Multiple 5xxs observed for routing to eu-west model pool. Pager duty triggered. (alert_id: alert-1741122334)
oncall-sre: acked. I'm looking. Seeing spike ~ 23:12 UTC in edge logs for region fallback failures.
laura.p: can you paste the edge error pattern?
oncall-sre: paste logs: ```ERROR: route_select: fallback loop detected, tried variants: [gptx-7b-q8, gptx-7b-q4, gptx-3b-quant] count=12```
michael.t: that matches an earlier misconfig where fallback_order included a deprecated variant that stopped answering health checks.
raj.k: I'm seeing DNS timeouts in edge-proxy for eu-west. `dig +short model-eu.redwood.internal` returns old IP 10.10.1.5 on some nodes, new IP 10.10.8.22 on others. TTL in zone is 3600.
ops-gw: confirmed. Edge caches still have stale endpoints in multiple POPs. Cloudflare cache-control shows TTL override 3600s.
oncall-sre: this explains the mixed routing; some edge nodes hit retired variant, health-check fails, triggers fallback policy which in turn prefers other regions -> cascade.
laura.p: customer impact?
oncall-sre: initial estimate: ~40% of eu-west requests saw >500ms added latency and 10% got 5xx during the window. Affected models mostly inference on gptx-7b variants.
customer-support: we've received 7 escalation tickets from large customers in EU complaining about intermittent failures and degraded throughput.
michael.t: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) reduce DNS TTL to 60s, 2) purge edge caches for model-eu host, 3) temporarily pin eu-west routing to stable pool with explicit IPs.
oncall-sre: I'm running purge now: `curl -X POST https://edge-api/purge -d '{"host":"model-eu.redwood.internal"}'` (resp 202).
deploy-bot: Deploy event: routing-policy rollback to v2 (legacy-fallback) requested by laura.p at 23:16 UTC — in progress.
raj.k: I can update zone TTL but that takes time to propagate. If we add `host: 10.10.8.22` to local edge host override on eu-west nodes we can stop the loop immediately.
laura.p: do it. push a config change to edge-config with high-priority host override and then revert once DNS flush completes.
ops-gw: applying host override via SRE-runbook: ```for node in $(cat eu-west-nodes); do ssh $node 'echo "10.10.8.22 model-eu.redwood.internal" >> /etc/hosts'; done```
oncall-sre: hosts updated on 12/14 nodes so far. health checks on retired variant are no longer being hit on those nodes.
michael.t: I'm lowering the zone TTL to 60 now: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://ttl-60.json`. Change submitted (chg-0x9a).
incident-bot: Note: Related incidents: routing-policy misconfig 1739990000.
laura.p: good call rolling back to v2. Any risk to other regions?
oncall-sre: v2 routing policy keeps region affinity and avoids cross-region failover loops. We need to monitor for any increase in load on eu-west stable pool.
raj.k: CDN purge completed for 16 POPs. `dig` now returns 10.10.8.22 consistently from our probe set.
customer-support: I told customers we're investigating and applied a mitigation; will update in 30m.
michael.t: metrics look normalizing — 5xx rate down from peak 4.2% to 0.8% over last 8 minutes. Latency back to baseline for eu-west nodes with host overrides.
oncall-sre: starting handoff notes for next-oncall: cause = stale DNS entries + fallback policy that escalated to cross-region routing and encountered deprecated variant causing loop. Mitigations applied: hosts override on eu-west, CDN purge, routing-policy rollback to v2, TTL lowered to 60. Open actions: verify Route53 propagation (chg-0x9a), remove host overrides once propagation confirmed, add TTL runbook, add alert for mixed-IP responses from DNS probes.
next-oncall: ack. I'll monitor route-select errors and verify for 30m.
laura.p: postmortem owners: raj for DNS change/automation, michael for routing policy rollbacks/QA, laura for runbook updates and customer comms.
incident-bot: Incident SEV2 -> resolved for now at 23:27 UTC. Please file postmortem and link to this thread. :white_check_mark:
customer-support: updated customers with resolution and ETA for postmortem.
raj.k: follow-up note: TTL change accepted and propagated to most resolvers; some ISP caches still honoring old TTL until their refresh window. Will remove hosts overrides in 15m if no regressions.
oncall-sre: removing host overrides in 10 nodes now.
michael.t: keep alert thresholds adjusted; disabled the fallback escalation rule temporarily until we fix policy validation to block deprecated variants.
laura.p: reminder for postmortem: include exact config diff for routing-policy v3 -> v2 rollback, timeline for DNS change, and proposed automation to detect stale endpoints in edge.
next-oncall: ack, taking over monitoring.
incident-bot: HANDOFF: next-oncall assigned 23:28 UTC.
laura.p: thanks everyone.
